81463.subject: Anthropic IPO: The Profit Is Real. Above $1.5 Trillion, the Price Isn't 🤖
81463.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/anthropic-ipo-s1-analysis-valuation

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
AI giant Anthropic finally made its S-1 public on Monday. The price range is still blank, but the people who will set it are already talking, and the number is falling. On filing day, Bloomberg reported that investors had moved their fair-value estimate down to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion after the company’s investor day [ https://substack.com/redirect/64fdb418-b47b-4bf5-8eb1-0c88674cc462?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], according to people familiar with the matter. Some of them said closer to $1.75 trillion is potentially achievable. The WSJ, also citing people familiar with the matter, had $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion. The raise could be as much as $100 billion. And just 5 months ago, Anthropic’s last private round valued it at $965 billion 🤯
The filing tells the story of a company that has just grown into its compute bill, and now has to keep outgrowing it.
→ The turn. Revenue went from $41 million in 2023 to $4.6 billion in 2025, then $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 alone. In Q2, Anthropic posted its first operating profit in the six quarters the filing shows: $974 million. Compute and infrastructure cost 1,056% of revenue in 2023. In Q2, it was 48% 🚀
→ The bill. At 30 June, Anthropic owed $267.7 billion under non-cancelable commitments, 13.6 times its trailing 12-month revenue. On top of that sit $321.4B of signed leases that are estimated or partly conditional. Google, Amazon and Microsoft get paid “regardless of actual usage” 😬 (The $800B+ in the headlines adds every contract together, ceilings and estimates included. More on that below.)
→ The revenue. 80% of it is consumption-based, and many of the largest customers have no long-term contract. We can remember that back in June, Washington switched off Anthropic’s two most advanced models for 18 days. The bills kept running.
And then there is the governance. One Class F share, held by the seven co-founders, carries a fixed 50.1% of the vote. A trust elects 4 of the 7 directors. In the filing’s own words, Class A holders “generally will not be able to affect” outcomes.
What’s interesting is what else the S-1 discloses: a compute deal with SpaceX [ https://substack.com/redirect/36861232-bdc3-47cd-afa4-2e288a8dc97a?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] worth up to $120.5 billion that either side can walk away from on 90 days’ notice from early 2027, an estimated 5% to 7% of 9-month revenue earned from customers breaking its usage policies, an $80.7B first-half net loss that is almost entirely accounting, and 5% of the company handed to a Public Benefit Fund run by 3 co-founde
